summary: Use a Step for one stage of a process inside a Stepper, such as Verify PAN, with its number or outcome and a line of detail.

useWhen.text: One stage of a process inside a Stepper, such as Verify PAN, with its number or outcome and a line of detail.

from.quote: Use a Step for one stage of a process inside a Stepper, such as Verify PAN, with its number or outcome and a line of detail.

avoidWhen.text: Placing a stage on its own in Figma: Step itself is a subcomponent in Coin Subcomponents, which designers don't use directly; designers place Steps through Stepper.

from.quote: Step itself is a subcomponent in Coin Subcomponents, which designers don’t use directly.

avoidWhen.text: The stage needs to be pressed or focused: Step is not interactive.

from.quote: Not interactive: no focus, no press.

placementAdvice.text: In Figma, place Steps through Stepper in the Components Library.

from.quote: In Figma, designers place Steps through Stepper in the Components Library

placementAdvice.text: A Step fills its column and is at least 52 px tall.

from.quote: A Step fills its column and is at least 52 px tall.

placementAdvice.text: The current stage can hold its own action, such as an Upload button, in its children.

from.quote: The current stage holds its own Upload button.

placementAdvice.text: In the guide's Form 16 example, uploading marks the stage done and the screen moves the current stage on.

from.quote: Uploading marks the stage done, and the screen moves the current stage on.

configuration.text: Every Step has a title: set title, unless children replace the text block and the title prop.

from.quote: Every Step has a title.

configuration.text: Use the title alone when it says enough; it is compact.

from.quote: Compact, when the title says enough.

configuration.text: Add supporting text when it helps, to say what the stage involves or how it went.

from.quote: Add supporting text and a date when they help

configuration.text: When it helps, add a date (metaText) for when the stage finished, started, or is due.

from.quote: When the stage finished, started, or is due.

configuration.text: Pass children to replace the text block and the title prop with your own content; the row and its connector grow.

from.quote: Children replace the text block and the title prop; the row and its connector grow.

configuration.text: Set showLine false on a Step you place yourself, outside a Stepper; inside a Stepper, Stepper turns it off on the last stage.

from.quote: Stepper turns it off on the last stage; turn it off on a Step you place yourself.

configuration.text: Inside a Stepper, the Stepper passes each Step its index, isCurrent and showLine.

from.quote: Inside a Stepper, each Step gets its index, the Stepper's modes (its own win), `isCurrent` on the first step that isn't complete, and no connector on the last step.

configuration.text: Set status to set the glyph and colour together.

from.quote: A Step’s status sets its glyph and colour together

configuration.text: Set the Step Status mode to inactive on an upcoming stage.

from.quote: an upcoming stage needs the Step Status mode set to inactive.

configuration.text: If you set Step Status explicitly, keep it matched to the status: an explicit Step Status always wins.

from.quote: An explicit Step Status always wins, so keep it matched to the status.

configuration.text: Do not set Step Status active on a done stage: an explicit Step Status of active overrides the green.

from.quote: An explicit Step Status of active overrides the green.

configuration.text: On the last Step you place yourself, turn off the connector: a connector with no next stage looks unfinished (inside a Stepper, Stepper does this).

from.quote: A connector with no next stage looks unfinished.

rules.text: One stage: its name, its state, and what happened.

from.quote: One stage: its name, its state, and what happened.

rules.text: Write the title as the stage in a few words, such as “Verify PAN”, not an action.

from.quote: Write the title as the stage in a few words, such as “Verify PAN”, not an action.

rules.text: Use the supporting text for what happens or what went wrong, and the date for when.

from.quote: Use the supporting text for what happens or what went wrong, and the date for when.

rules.text: Say in the text why a stage failed: the glyph only says that it failed, not why.

from.quote: The glyph only says that a stage failed, not why.

rules.text: Do not leave the default title: “Stepper Item” tells people nothing, and it's read as “Step 1”.

from.quote: “Stepper Item” tells people nothing, and it’s read as “Step 1”.

from.quote: Screen readers hear the title, supporting text of up to 80 characters, and the date.

examples.purpose: Filing an ITR: the current stage holds its own Upload button in its children, and the upcoming stage is inactive.
examples.jsx:
<Stepper accessibilityLabel="File your ITR" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }}>
  <Step title="Verify PAN" supportingText="PAN details match your name" metaText="Done 2 Oct 2026" status="complete" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }} />
  <Step modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }}>
    <StepLabel title="Upload Form 16" supportingText="Add the PDF from your employer" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }} />
    <Button label="Upload" onPress={() => {}} modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light', 'Button / Size': 'S' }} />
  </Step>
  <Step title="Review and submit" supportingText="Check your income and file" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light', 'Step Status': 'inactive' }} />
</Stepper>

from.quote: The current stage holds its own Upload button.

props.name: children
props.description: Replace the default StepLabel and get Step's modes; the Step's own title and date are then ignored, and a StepLabel child's title, supporting text and date make the name.

props.name: index
props.description: Default 0; the number shows index + 1. Inside a Stepper each Step gets its index. Declared: Default 0, from the component source.

props.name: showLine
props.description: Stepper sets it false on the last step; a standalone Step keeps index 0, a connector, and no current marker unless set. Declared: Default true, from the component source.

props.name: title
props.description: StepLabel shows “Stepper Item” when title is unset.

props.name: metaText
props.description: The date; screen readers read it with the title, the supporting text and the outcome word.

props.name: subtitle
props.description: Default true; false hides the supporting text. Declared: Default true, from the component source.

props.name: meta
props.description: Default true; false hides the date. Declared: Default true, from the component source.

props.name: status
props.description: Sets the glyph, and the colour when no Step Status mode is set (complete green, error red, warning orange); an explicit Step Status still wins. Declared: Default "number", from the component source.

props.name: isCurrent
props.description: Set by Stepper on the first step that isn't complete; on the web the Step then has aria-current="step". Declared: Set by Stepper: this is the current incomplete step. Default false, from the component source.

props.name: withinStepper
props.description: Set by Stepper; then the Step is a list item (with aria-current when current). A Step on its own is a group with the same name. Declared: Set by Stepper. Standalone Steps are not list items. Default false, from the component source.

modes.name: Color Mode
modes.description: A token collection Step reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

modes.name: Step Status
modes.description: Overrides the colour status picks; upcoming lavender (inactive) only comes from this mode. Declared: A token collection Step reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

gaps.text: The status glyph is an unnamed image on the web rather than hidden; the title and status word carry the meaning.
